card.summary: A two‑story cream‑brick colonial home with a large front porch, four bedrooms, two baths, and a two‑car garage, built to 1920s pattern‑book proportions.
card.description: The residence presents a dignified colonial silhouette rendered in warm cream brick, its 1372 cm wide façade capped by a steep gabled shingle roof that echoes early‑20th‑century pattern‑book homes. Two full stories rise above a 15 cm thick concrete slab, each level offering 2.44 m tall rooms that balance proportion and comfort. A generous front porch stretches 183 cm outward, its concrete floor and timber‑framed gable inviting occupants to linger beneath the overhanging eaves. The front entry is marked by a solid wood door on a hinged frame, while fifteen double‑hung windows punctuate the brick walls, each sliding to admit fresh air. A two‑car garage occupies the left side, its steel roll‑up door providing modern convenience. Inside, four bedrooms and two full baths are arranged around a central hallway, with a staircase of timber treads linking the floors. Interior doors and trim are crafted from seasoned wood, and the living spaces are finished with hardwood flooring and plaster ceilings. All mechanical systems are concealed within the wall cavities and attic, preserving the clean lines of the exterior while delivering contemporary comfort.

card.summary: A two‑story colonial home with a large front porch, four bedrooms, two baths, and built‑in rocking chair, changing table, and nightlight.
card.description: The residence is a two‑story colonial‑style home measuring 1280 cm wide by 991 cm deep, with 244 cm ceiling heights on each floor. White wood clapboard siding wraps the structure, while a gabled asphalt‑shingle roof crowns the building with a 30 cm overhang. A generous front porch, 400 cm deep, spans the full façade, supported by a concrete pad and timber joists, and is topped by a matching gable roof. The interior features four bedrooms and two full baths, hardwood floors throughout the main level, and plastered ceilings. Colonial proportions dictate evenly spaced double‑hung windows (10 of them) and a solid wood front door with a hinge. The house is built on a 20 cm thick concrete slab foundation, with timber framing, plywood sheathing, and house wrap for weather resistance. Mechanical systems are concealed within the ceiling and walls, delivering forced‑air heating and modern electrical lighting. Furnishings include a handcrafted wooden rocking chair in the living room, a wooden changing table in a dedicated nursery, and a low‑profile plastic nightlight mounted beside the crib. The design balances historic charm with contemporary livability, presenting a stately yet welcoming presence on the empty lot.

card.description: This single‑storey colonial bungalow measures 792 cm wide by 1417 cm deep and rises 300 cm from the ground to the ridge of its modest shingled roof. The white‑painted shingle walls are framed with 2×6 timber studs, giving the façade a crisp, orderly rhythm of evenly spaced double‑hung windows and a centered front door. A modest front porch, 200 cm wide and 300 cm deep, provides a sheltered transition from the gate to the entry, its wooden railing echoing the simple elegance of the period. To the right of the solid‑wood front door stands a freestanding steel coat rack, 40 cm wide, 30 cm deep, and 150 cm tall, its four hinged hooks ready to receive outerwear as guests arrive. Inside, the layout follows the classic 1920s pattern‑book plan: a spacious living room, a kitchen with built‑in cabinets, three modest bedrooms, and a single bathroom, all served by a central hallway. The roof is clad in traditional asphalt shingles, and the entire structure rests on a reinforced concrete slab foundation, ensuring durability for generations. Every element—from the mailbox on the porch to the interior doors—has been proportioned to respect the historic colonial aesthetic while providing modern comfort.
